title: apps/provisioning/pkg — architecture & control-flow map
answers: Where does provisioning admission/mutation get wired up?
How does a Repository/Connection get built from its CRD?
Where is the composition root for provisioning extras?
body:
apps/provisioning is a separate Go module (own go.mod, listed in go.work) holding the provisioning app's API types (`pkg/apis/provisioning/v0alpha1/types.go`, generated from CUE in `apps/provisioning/kinds/*.cue`), admission plumbing (`pkg/apis/admission/`), the `Repository`/`Connection` abstractions + backend impls (`pkg/repository/`, `pkg/repository/git|github|local`, `pkg/connection/`), and status-patch helpers (`pkg/controller/status.go`). It does NOT run jobs/workers or expose the HTTP API — that lives in the main module at `pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/` (jobs drivers, webhooks, storage), which depends on this module, never the reverse.

Composition root: `pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/extras/register.go:ProvideProvisioningOSSRepositoryExtras` builds the `repository.Extra`/`connection.Extra` list (local/git/github) and feeds `repository.ProvideFactory` (apps/provisioning/pkg/repository/factory.go:ProvideFactory) and `connection.ProvideFactory` (apps/provisioning/pkg/connection/factory.go:ProvideFactory). `pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/register.go` (~line 844) creates `admission.NewHandler()` (apps/provisioning/pkg/apis/admission/admission.go:NewHandler) and registers per-resource Mutator/Validator for Repository, Connection, Job.

Inbound flow: API-server admission on Repository/Connection/Job → `admission.Handler.Mutate/Validate` dispatches by resource name → `repository.Factory.Mutate/Validate` or `connection.Factory.Mutate/Validate` → dispatches by `Spec.Type` to the matching `Extra` (e.g. apps/provisioning/pkg/repository/git/extra.go:extra.Validate).
Outbound flow: `repository.Factory.Build` (apps/provisioning/pkg/repository/factory.go) is the single chokepoint every caller (job drivers, HTTP handlers, controllers in pkg/registry/apis/provisioning) uses to construct a live Repository; `controller.RepositoryStatusPatcher.Patch` (apps/provisioning/pkg/controller/status.go) writes job/sync results back onto the CR status subresource via the generated typed client.

search: apps/provisioning is a separate Go module (go.mod, go.work) that holds API types, admission plumbing, Repository/Connection abstractions, and status-patch helpers, but does NOT run jobs or expose HTTP API — that responsibility belongs to pkg/registry/apis/provisioning in the main module, which depends on apps/provisioning but never reverse. Entry points are ProvideFactory functions (apps/provisioning/pkg/repository/factory.go:ProvideFactory, apps/provisioning/pkg/connection/factory.go:ProvideFactory), NewHandler (apps/provisioning/pkg/apis/admission/admission.go:NewHandler), RepositoryStatusPatcher (apps/provisioning/pkg/controller/status.go), and the composition root ProvideProvisioningOSSRepositoryExtras (pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/extras/register.go). The inbound flow dispatches API-server admission on Repository/Connection/Job to matching backends by Spec.Type; the outbound flow funnels all Repository construction through repository.Factory.Build and status writes through RepositoryStatusPatcher.Patch. Apply this to understand control flow in provisioning subsystem and avoid circular dependencies between modules.
